names.kinematic_iteration_endpoint: arm_chain.py's former 'fixed point' (Arm.aim): the action decoder's arm-group step (stacked damped least squares of the wrist position row weighted 8 and the wrist, lower-arm and upper-arm orientation rows, each times its handle's strength, lambda 0.001, every hinge step clipped to its range) iterated from the recorded pose at world record t-1 with the free root, the trunk hinges and the other arm held; each iteration scaled so the largest hinge change is at most 0.10 rad; 'converged' = the largest change fell below 1e-5 rad before 200 iterations; 'unfinished' = 200 iterations ran without that. Not the pose the body attains: forces, gravity, joint springs, contacts, fatigue and the 250 ms hold are absent from the iteration.
names.records_near_observed_command_extreme: former 'rail_records': hold records (one per model step, 5 per hold) in which an arm actuator's recorded command (ctrl) is at least 99.5% of the largest command recorded in that direction over the body's own records in the loaded tracks; an observed extreme, not a declared limit
names.records_at_declared_command_bound: hold records in which an arm actuator's recorded ctrl is at least 99.5% of its declared bound in that direction: the actuator's forcerange in MIMo_metav2.xml, the bound MIMo's SpringDamperModel sets as the action space and env.step clips ctrl to; force = gear x capacity x ctrl (env._apply_motor_function scales the gain and the force range by the set's fatigue capacity), so a command at its bound asks the largest force the fatigued actuator gives
names.palm_to_box_root_under_9cm_count: former 'aim_end_below_9cm' and 'box_root_within_9cm': holds whose palm origin lies under 9 cm from the box root, a distance count only; 9 cm is the median palm-origin-to-box-root distance at the end of reach acts with hand contact (trace end_distance_cm_median_with_contact 8.9 cm), never a contact line
names.contact: a MuJoCo contact between a body of the hand (palm or finger) or arm of the named side and a geom of the named object in a world record (observer contact rows); arm_chain counts records with such a contact per hold (arm or hand), the traces list contact events with onset model step, continuous duration and peak force (hand only)
names.body_index_zero_based: world folder b0..b7 = the trainer's body index 0..7; 'body 5' everywhere here is b5
names.sign_agreement: the decoder replica's command signs agree with the recorded arm ctrl on 99.6% of 67,809 (B1E) and 68,268 (seg41r) pairs: support for the local direction of the decoder step on recorded poses, not for force magnitude, endpoint accuracy or dynamic equivalence

corrected_claims: The arm attribution's 'fixed point' is a kinematic iteration endpoint; where the recorded command's iteration ended unfinished (200 iterations without the 1e-5 rad stop), its endpoint is reported apart and is not called a fixed point or the pose the servo attains.

The 'rail' count is the count of records near the observed command extreme; saturation is claimed only from records_at_declared_command_bound (MIMo_metav2.xml's forcerange), and only where no recorded command lies beyond that declared bound.

The old 'every fixed point puts the palm farther from the box than it already was' is not true of every hold: among converged kinematic iteration endpoints of planner holds inside the 45 cm filter, the endpoint lies farther from the box root than the start in 25 of 52 (B1E zero-based body 1) to 49 of 59 (seg41r body 1) holds per body.

The old 'every fixed point is farther from the goal palm than the start' is not true of every hold: among the same converged endpoints with a goal ring entry, the endpoint lies farther from the goal palm than the start in 63 of 99 (B1E zero-based body 4) to 75 of 92 (seg41r body 6) holds per body; the medians are farther in every body.
9 cm is a median palm-origin-to-box-root distance at the end of reach acts with hand contact; touches are contact records and contact events with durations.
The first arm_goal_check run (INVALID) stands; its failing self-tests are the range clip of remembered arm hinges that lay beyond their ranges, with the palm displacement listed per hold.
Repeated command signs support the local direction of the decoder step, not force magnitude or dynamic equivalence.
Gains and fatigue are not changed by this evidence (the decision's text).

B1E b1 box_light.note: declared bound = MIMo_metav2.xml's forcerange, the action space env.step clips ctrl to; records_at_declared_command_bound is null where a recorded ctrl lies beyond it (no saturation claimed there). saved_model_range_over_declared: the observer saves ONE world model file per run's kinematic structure (saved_model; every body of the run reads the same file), holding the range scaled by each body set's fatigue capacity of the world that wrote it when it was saved (env._apply_motor_function), so the ratio is that one file's capacity at that time, not this body's capacity during the window
